newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan's Nan Ya Technology plans DRAM expansion.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's Nan Ya Technology plans DRAM expansion.

text.p: Taiwan semiconductor maker Nan Ya Technology Corp, a subsidiary of Nan Ya Plastics, said on Friday it planned to expand its dynamic random-access memory chip production but declined to give details.
"Keeping up investment in expansion is inevitable in DRAM manufacturing, and Nan Ya Technology is no exception," a company executive, who declined to be named, told Reuters.
"We do plan to invest more in the future, but details have yet to be set," he said.
The executive declined to confirm a report in Friday's Economic Daily News that Nan Ya Technology would invest T$20 billion to build a second DRAM plant in northern Linkou.
Nan Ya Technology, which was founded in 1994 to build a US$675 million DRAM plant, is wholly owned by Formosa Plastics Group.
DRAM chips are a key computer component.
The first DRAM plant began operation in May 1996, the executive said.
"We expect to turn out 22,000 eight-inch wafers of DRAMs a month in 1997, exceeding our designed monthly capacity of 20,000 wafers," he said.
Nan Ya now produces 16-megabit DRAMs and will begin 64-MB production once market demand justifies such a move, he said.
